subject: How can I model the sequence of servicing the customers in simmer?

messages.author: 74241b5ea0393aa5
messages.subject: How can I model the sequence of servicing the customers in simmer?
parts: Assume we have indefinite customers in a system with different types, I want to simulate different patterns for serving the customers. for example, type 1 then type 2 then type 3 then type 1 ... in Mondays.My question is how I should model the sequence of servicing the customers? I need to define different patterns for serving the customers and evaluate the resource utilization.

I'm not sure what are you trying to achieve. E.g., what happens if you
implement the 1-2-3 pattern and only type 1 and 3 arrive? Does it stop
until a type 2 arrives?

--

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] How can I model the sequence of servicing the customers in simmer?
parts:
On Sat, 8 Dec 2018 at 18:29, Narges Shahraki <nsha...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Inaki,
>
> Thank you very much for your response. Yes, let's assume the resource stops until a type 2 arrives. I want to evaluate changing the patterns of servicing different customer types on waiting times and resource utilization.

Then I would use auxiliary resources as token buckets. E.g. (not tested):

main <- trajectory() %>%
seize("resource") %>%
timeout(service) %>%
release("resource") %>%
select(paste0("type", 1:3), "round-robin") %>%
set_capacity_selected(1)

type1 <- trajectory() %>%
seize("type1") %>%
set_capacity("type1", 0) %>%
join(main) %>%
release("type1")

type2 <- trajectory() %>%
...

type3 <- trajectory() %>%
...

Instead of "round-robin", you can provide your own R function to
implement any policy you want. There's a quite sophisticated example
of this pattern in the following vignette:

https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-aa-5g#mobile-traffic-backhauling-with-fttx

--
Iñaki Úcar
